item.title: How Small Postgres Metadata Tables Quietly Throttle Your Largest Queries
item.content:encoded: Most engineers blame slow time-series queries on massive fact tables, but a small metadata table with stale Postgres statistics can silently become the real bottleneck. This guide shows how outdated ANALYZE data misleads the planner into choosing inefficient joins, how to detect row-estimate mismatches with EXPLAIN, and how to fix them using autovacuum tuning, targeted audits, or selective denormalization.

item.title: No AI Agent Without Identity (Part 5): Auditability and the Minimum Bar for Governed Autonomy
item.content:encoded: Part 5 of a 5-part series on agentic AI governance. This article defines the minimum bar for governed AI autonomy: stable agent identity, ownership, runtime lineage, policy decisions, supervision mode, credential control, revocation behavior, audit evidence, and accountability across human, agent, tool, and context chains.

item.title: The Compounding Latency Crisis of Multi-Step AI Workflows
item.content:encoded: Chaining multiple LLM calls, vector database lookups, and API tools creates a severe performance bottleneck, dragging response times from seconds to minutes. Every sequential step introduces extra network and token processing overhead that quickly ruins the user experience. To fix this compounding latency crisis, engineers must move away from rigid, blocking sequential code. Instead, you need to use smaller, faster models for minor tasks, run speculative database lookups in parallel while models are still thinking, and stream real-time status updates back to the UI to keep the application feeling crisp and responsive.

item.title: Why Global Fetch Defaults Can Leak API Tokens
item.content:encoded: Global API defaults can silently leak auth headers across services. Here’s how isolated client configs prevent that risk.

item.title: The Hidden Liability Behind AI-Assisted Coding
item.content:encoded: The backlash against vibe coding is justified, just that the reasoning for it isn’t. Here’s the actual case against vibe coding no one is making.

item.title: No laptop? No problem. Code on the Go brings the debugger to your phone.
item.content:encoded: Traditional Android debugging assumes you have both a computer and a phone. Code on the Go changes that by bringing the entire debugging workflow onto a single Android device. This post explains the technical challenges of building phone-native debugger, including privileged access, process management, and breakpoint handling, and how the team solved them while ensuring the debugger only works on the device running Code on the Go. The result is a fully self-contained Android development experience that lets developers write, build, run, and debug apps anywhere, without a laptop or internet connection.

item.title: How I Engineered a 1.7M Row Product Safety Database to Serve Pages in 66ms on a Single Free VM
item.content:encoded: How LemonKnows scaled 1.7M PostgreSQL rows, 41,000 recalls, and 7-language support on a free 6GB ARM server with 66ms page loads.

item.title: When APIs, Clients, and Infrastructure Are All Right—but the System Is Wrong
item.content:encoded: This article discusses key software engineering concepts, including development methodologies, testing, automation, code quality, and best practices for delivering scalable and maintainable software solutions.

item.title: How to Count Gemini Tokens Locally
item.content:encoded: This article explores how Gemini tokenizes data and demonstrates how to count or estimate tokens locally. You'll learn how to use the local tokenizer to estimate text token counts offline, understand the tokenization math for multimodal inputs (images, audio, video, PDFs), and see how to retrieve precise token usage metadata from API responses for accurate tracking and billing.

item.title: Fraud Has Moved Outside the Bank. Protection Should Too
item.content:encoded: Banks are investing heavily in cybersecurity and fraud detection, but AI-powered social engineering attacks increasingly happen outside their systems through calls, messages, emails, and social media. Leading institutions like JPMorgan and Revolut are expanding protections with consumer education, scam detection, and intervention tools, yet most defenses still focus on the moment before a transaction occurs. As regulations tighten and fraud losses grow, banks need to move beyond their perimeter and deploy device-level trust layers that can understand communication context, detect scams earlier, and leverage cross-industry threat intelligence to keep pace with AI-enabled fraud at scale.
